title: The Gospels — Walking with Jesus
description: Test your understanding of the life, ministry, teachings, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ as recorded in the four Gospels.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophet foretold that the Messiah would be born of a virgin in Bethlehem?
options: Jeremiah predicted both the virgin birth and the birthplace
Isaiah prophesied the virgin birth (Isaiah 7:14), and Micah prophesied Bethlehem as the birthplace (Micah 5:2)
Daniel predicted the virgin birth and the birthplace
Moses foretold the exact details of Jesus' birth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:14 prophesied the virgin birth ('the virgin will conceive'), and Micah 5:2 named Bethlehem as the birthplace. These prophecies were written hundreds of years before Jesus was born.

questions.question: At Jesus' baptism, how were all three persons of the Trinity revealed?
options: Three angels appeared and spoke to Jesus
Jesus was baptized (the Son), the Holy Spirit descended like a dove, and the Father spoke from heaven
Moses, Elijah, and God all appeared at the Jordan River
Jesus spoke in three different voices
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:16-17 records that Jesus (the Son) was baptized, the Spirit descended like a dove, and the Father's voice declared, 'This is my Son, whom I love.' All three persons of the Trinity were present.

questions.question: How did Jesus defeat Satan's temptations in the wilderness?
options: He used His divine power to destroy Satan
He called angels to fight Satan for Him
He quoted Scripture each time, saying 'It is written'
He ignored Satan until he went away
questions.explanation: Jesus responded to each of Satan's three temptations by quoting Scripture from the book of Deuteronomy. He showed us that God's Word is the primary weapon against temptation.

questions.question: In the Sermon on the Mount, what did Jesus teach about true righteousness?
options: That following the rules perfectly is enough to please God
That outward religious practices are more important than inner attitudes
That true righteousness goes beyond outward behavior to the attitudes of the heart
That the Old Testament Law no longer applies to Christians
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that true righteousness is a matter of the heart, not just external behavior. For example, He said that anger is the root of murder and lust is the root of adultery (Matthew 5:21-28).

questions.question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, what does the father's response to his returning son teach us about God?
options: That God punishes us severely when we disobey
That God reluctantly accepts us back if we prove ourselves
That God welcomes repentant sinners with joy, grace, and full restoration
That God does not care whether we obey Him or not
questions.explanation: The father ran to meet his son, embraced him, and threw a celebration — illustrating God's lavish grace toward those who repent and return to Him (Luke 15:20-24).

questions.question: Why are Jesus' miracles called 'signs' in the Gospel of John?
options: Because they were performed using sign language
Because they pointed beyond themselves to reveal Jesus' identity as the Son of God
Because they were meant to entertain the crowds
Because only certain people could see them
questions.explanation: John 20:30-31 explains that Jesus' miracles were recorded as signs 'that you may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God.' Each miracle pointed to a truth about who Jesus is.

questions.question: What is substitutionary atonement?
options: The belief that Jesus taught us how to save ourselves through good works
The doctrine that Jesus died in our place, taking the punishment for our sins so we could be forgiven
The idea that Jesus' death was an accident that God used for good
The teaching that everyone is automatically saved regardless of faith
questions.explanation: Substitutionary atonement means Jesus took our place on the cross, bearing the punishment we deserved. Isaiah 53:5 says, 'He was pierced for our transgressions... the punishment that brought us peace was on him.'

questions.question: Why is the resurrection of Jesus the foundation of the Christian faith?
options: Because it proves Jesus was a good moral teacher
Because it is a nice story that gives people hope
Because it proves Jesus is the Son of God, that His sacrifice was accepted, and that believers will also be raised to eternal life
Because it showed that Jesus could escape from any situation
questions.explanation: Paul wrote that 'if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile' (1 Corinthians 15:17). The resurrection vindicates Jesus' identity, confirms His atoning work, and guarantees eternal life for all believers.
